healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private (Social Health Insurance for residents)
qualityNotes: Healthcare varies dramatically between major cities and rural areas. Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have good private international clinics and hospitals with English-speaking staff. Public hospitals are overcrowded and often lack English. Private healthcare is affordable by Western standards.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (nhà thuốc) are extremely common in cities and towns, often open 24/7. Many medications are available without prescription, including antibiotics.
pharmacyTips: Vietnam has very easy pharmacy access — many medications available OTC that require prescriptions elsewhere, including antibiotics. However, quality of medications can be inconsistent. Buy from reputable pharmacies (large chains like Long Chau, Pharmacity, or Nexus) when possible.
prescriptionRules: Many medications are available OTC. For prescription drugs, a Vietnamese doctor's prescription may be required. International prescriptions are generally not accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Some products may be available with a prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. A Vietnamese prescription is required.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid pain medications
restrictedMeds.note: Strong painkillers are controlled and require a prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Vietnam. Penalties are severe.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Bring sufficient supply in original packaging. For any controlled medications, carry documentation. Some medications may require a specific import permit from Vietnamese authorities.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required for most nationalities, but strongly recommended.
travelInsurance.tips: International clinics in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City accept direct billing from major insurers. Public hospitals require payment upfront. Medical evacuation from rural areas to Bangkok or Singapore may be necessary for serious conditions. Ensure your policy covers this.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers, but Hepatitis A and Typhoid are recommended for most visitors.

waterNotes: Do not drink tap water in Vietnam. Drink bottled water only. Use bottled water for brushing teeth. Ice in drinks at reputable restaurants is generally safe (made from purified water).
foodSafetyTips: Vietnamese street food is world-famous and mostly safe from popular, busy stalls. Pho (noodle soup), banh mi, and spring rolls are safe. Avoid raw salads (may be washed in tap water) — eat only cooked vegetables. Be cautious with undercooked pork (common in bún chả). Shellfish from street vendors in hot weather can be risky.
medicalTourismNote: Vietnam is developing as a a medical tourism destination, particularly for dental work and cosmetic surgery, at significantly lower costs than Western countries.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Vietnam. Emergency numbers (115, 113), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, and travel insurance advice.

hospitals.name: FV Hospital
hospitals.notes: International-standard hospital. English and French speaking. JCI-accredited.

hospitals.name: Vinmec International Hospital
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Multiple locations — Hanoi, HCMC, Nha Trang, Da Nang
hospitals.notes: Vietnam's premier private hospital chain. International patient services.

hospitals.name: Family Medical Practice
hospitals.nearTouristArea: District 1, HCMC / Old Quarter, Hanoi / Da Nang
hospitals.notes: International clinic chain. Walk-in and emergency services. Highly recommended for tourists.

hospitals.name: Hoan My Da Nang Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital serving central Vietnam's tourist region.

dentalCare.availability: Dental care in major cities is good and very affordable. HCMC and Hanoi have international-standard clinics.
dentalCare.costRange: $10-30 for consultation; $20-60 for fillings; $15-50 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Vietnam is an emerging dental tourism destination. Elite Dental, Westcoast International, and Dr. Hung dental clinics in HCMC are popular with foreigners. Quality varies widely — choose carefully.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: FV Hospital and Vinmec have dental departments for emergencies. Family Medical Practice clinics can provide referrals.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy for English-language crisis support
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited. Some available through FV Hospital and Family Medical Practice in HCMC and Hanoi.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services in English are very limited in Vietnam. International clinics in HCMC and Hanoi offer psychiatric services. For serious mental health concerns, consider medical evacuation to Bangkok or Singapore.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Vietnam's accessibility is very limited. Sidewalks are often blocked by motorbikes, streets are chaotic, and most buildings lack wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: International hospitals (FV, Vinmec) are wheelchair accessible. Public hospitals have limited access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Grab (ride-hailing) is the best option. Traffic is chaotic — crossing streets is challenging for anyone.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi's old quarters are extremely challenging for wheelchair users. Newer areas and resorts are more accessible. Hire a guide for assistance. Ha Long Bay cruises vary in accessibility — confirm before booking.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Some indoor venues may request masks.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at hospitals and clinics. Cost: $10-30 for PCR.
covidStatus.notes: Vietnam removed all COVID entry restrictions. Dengue fever and food/water safety are more relevant health concerns.

insuranceClaimProcess: International hospitals accept direct billing from some insurers. Local facilities require upfront cash payment. Keep all receipts (hóa đơn) and medical reports. Family Medical Practice and FV Hospital provide English documentation as standard. File claims promptly.
